finding: Committing runner publication outputs can advance HEAD through runner-affecting paths, causing taskflow pre-close to mark the just-published runner-sync receipt as rebuild-required and forcing a second sealed build/publication cycle.
expectedBehavior: Runner-sync publication should converge in one governed transaction, or classify publication-only commits so dist/release output commits do not recursively invalidate their own receipt when the source input tree remains semantically sealed.
evidenceOrRepro: During ATM-GOV-0252, runner-sync release for sealed source 56a506b3e was blocked by ATM_RUNNER_PUBLICATION_PENDING. After an exact pathspec publication commit 02ad794d, pre-close reported runnerReceiptPublicationClosure.status=rebuild-required because HEAD advanced through packages/cli/dist/commands/tasks/close-orchestrator/closure-packet.js. A second build and second publication commit e491455c were required before the receipt was accepted.
followUp: Design a single canonical publication transaction or receipt supersession rule that separates source input sealing from release-output publication commits, with regression coverage for package dist plus release manifest updates.
